chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: A band job: Eagles Ballroom in Milwaukee and Gull Lake
summary: Booked by Stevens and Wirth, he fronts the house band in Milwaukee and a Notre Dame band at Gull Lake, Michigan, learning to emcee and dance.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So, now I'm doing a single, I'm up to the part I'm doing a single. Now all the time I'm doing a single, I keep saying, I want to work with a band.
So I -- we knew a booking agent, Stevens and With in Chicago --
Right. And so they said, 'Well I don't know how we can get you with a band.' I said, this unless you're like a novelty thing. Novelty -- as far as the band's concerned.

And I said, 'Well I don't know what to say. What do you think I can do?' I said, 'Well I don't know.' But they liked what I did -- what I was trying to do. So they finally got me a job at Eagle's Ballroom in Milwaukee. IN front of the house band. Now we're playing -- there's two bands. There's a house band and Charlie Bollinger's band on the other side, which was a great band. A great band, swing band, jazz band. About 12-14 men. And we had a big band, so they made me director. And I stood out in front and I was scared to death, I said what am I directing, they said don't worry about it -- just stand there, I mean, you're a nice looking little kid, get out there and play, and when they fade, why yell the tunes and get their tunes and play them.

So every -- during the evening, then I'd do a couple of specialties, and the people all call around and that's the way it started to work with bands. Now, finally this same office booked me in a place called Gull Lake, Michigan, with a band from Notre Dame. And I worked all summer and that was a great experience for me. Cause I really -- they had me in front of the band, now that band was organized, they had arrangements and they told me the tunes, and I learned the tunes and I played.
And then there was still dancing in those times, see. So I'd do a little dance number and play it at the same time -- and the ballroom that was as you know?

Then. And I'd set intermissions and do the the numbers -- announce the numbers. I learned how to talk a little bit in vaudeville, see. So it was a good experience for me. Now, all this time, I'm trying to -- trying to see where the light -- which way it's going to be for me to keep working on this kind of thing --
